page: OVHcloud b2-60 is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by the KVM hypervisor on an x86_64 architecture. The server is provisioned with 16 dedicated physical cores running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz on an Intel Haswell generation processor, operating without hyperthreading. System memory totals 60.0 GB, providing an allocation of 3.75 GB per core. The instance includes 400 GB of bundled local SSD storage and a baseline network interface speed of 1 Gbps. No graphical processing units are attached.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent multi-threaded throughput alongside modest single-threaded metrics. The instance achieves a PassMark CPU score of 18,774.29 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 7,339.0, both placing in the middle 50% tier of cloud instances. However, due to its older CPU architecture and modest base clock speed, single-core benchmarks such as Geekbench single-core (1,106.0) and stress-ng single-core (1,067.12) place in the bottom 25% bracket. Memory testing shows read bandwidth reaching 45.81 GB/sec on large blocks, whereas uncached write bandwidth settles lower at 20.8 GB/sec.

From an efficiency perspective, the dedicated 16-core allocation and 60.0 GB memory footprint provide predictable capacity for multi-threaded tasks, balanced by standard integrated local SSD storage. The trade-off centers on latency-sensitive and instruction-set-dependent tasks, as the CPU lacks AVX-512 extensions and modern cryptographic accelerators. Suitable workloads include parallel software compilation, medium-scale relational databases, Redis caching layers, web serving clusters, and batch data processing pipelines.
